description: The prefix key everything else hangs off
detail: Rebound from the default Ctrl+b. Easier to reach, and it does not fight vim's Ctrl+b page-up.

description: Split the pane left and right
detail: The new pane opens in the same directory as the one you split, so there is nothing to cd into.

description: Split the pane top and bottom
detail: Also inherits the current directory.

description: Move between panes, and in and out of neovim splits
detail: No prefix needed. vim-tmux-navigator makes the same four keys keep working once the pane is running neovim.

description: Resize the pane by 5 cells
detail: The binding repeats, so tap the letter again without pressing the prefix each time.

description: Zoom the pane to fill the window, press again to restore
detail: A zoomed window shows a marker next to its name in the status bar.

description: Flash the pane numbers, press one to jump there
Close this pane
detail: Asks for confirmation first.

description: Cycle through the built-in pane layouts
detail: Quick way to rebalance a messy split.

description: Break this pane out into its own window
New window, in the current directory
detail: Plain tmux would open it wherever the session started; this config keeps your path.

description: Jump to a window by number
detail: Numbering starts at 1, not 0, and renumbers itself when a window closes.

description: Rename this window
detail: Renaming also stops tmux from renaming it for you.

description: Move this window one slot left or right
Next / previous window
Close this window
Start a named session
Reattach to a session
detail: Plain `tmux a` picks up the most recent one.

description: Detach and leave everything running
Pick a session from a tree of all of them
Rename this session
Does not drop you back to the plain shell
detail: detach-on-destroy is off, so tmux moves you to another session instead of exiting.

description: Enter copy mode and scroll back through output
detail: Movement is vi style: / and ? to search, n, gg, G all work.

description: Select text, then copy it to the macOS clipboard
detail: y pipes the selection through pbcopy, so it lands in every app, not just tmux.

description: Paste what you last copied
detail: Capital P: lowercase p is already previous window.

description: Leave copy mode
Reload tmux.conf without restarting anything
Install the plugins listed in tmux.conf
detail: tpm bindings: Prefix + U updates them, Prefix + Alt+u removes ones you deleted from the config.

description: Type a tmux command directly
detail: Tab completes. Good for one-off things like `swap-window -t 1`.

description: Restore the sessions saved before the last reboot
detail: tmux-resurrect saves layouts and pane contents, tmux-continuum snapshots every 15 minutes.

description: A coding agent in that window is working
detail: The flag sits next to the window name in the status bar.

description: The agent finished and is waiting on you
The agent needs a permission answer before it can carry on
Agent session is open but idle
detail: The flag disappears entirely once the pane is back at a shell.
